# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *The Sea Around Us* that had been on the shelf since before Doreen started at the library. A soft pencil mark under the phrase "the long Atlantic swells," and in the margin, in small careful handwriting: *Pacific swells also long. See p. 87 of later editions.*

Doreen almost missed it. She was shelving returns on a Tuesday afternoon, the slow hour between the after-school rush and the evening regulars, when the light through the big windows went amber and the whole building smelled of salt and old paper. The harbor was visible from the circulation desk, a quarter mile down Main Street, where the fishing boats rocked against their moorings. She turned the page, saw the note, and frowned.

Patrons weren't supposed to write in library books. That was rule one, practically. But there was something in the handwriting—the humility of pencil, the smallness of it—that made her hesitate before reaching for the eraser.
